messages.subject: Re: Missing replicates
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Great question considering the case when a protein is entirely missing.  Referencing the MSstats V4 paper <https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00834>, "features are not imputed if a protein is entirely missing in a run".

So in the example you presented, if a protein is only detected in one replicate out of three, MSstats does NOT impute the missing replicates.

Tony

On Monday, June 30, 2025 at 4:19:00 PM UTC-4 lara.h...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello MSstats team,
>
> I have a question regarding imputation and the minimal values requred for the imputation.
> From what I recall, the decition to impute or not to impute relies on the amount of the features that each protein has in each sample. but what happens to proteins that has been detected in only one replicate out of three? or two replicate out of three? Will be the missing replicate imputed? Is there a command for setting up a minimal missing samples? If not, what is the build in rule for that?
>
> Thank you

messages.subject: Re: dataProcess issue
messages.body_plain:
Update on this thread:

For those who may encounter this, you may have rows where the FragmentIon column contains "precursor", "precursor [M+1]", etc, but for DIA/SRM datasets, those rows need to be removed for MSstats since MSstats performs differential abundance analysis at the fragment ion level (and not precursor level).

When exporting MSstats from Skyline, you can hit preview and filter out rows containing "precursor".  See screenshots.

Tony

messages.subject: Time-course study design annotation query
messages.body_plain:
Hello MSstats,

I am attempting to carty out a time-course MSstats analysis. I have attached a ppt file which displays my experimental design. I have 3 time-points, 2 treatments and 3 biological replicates of these. Using the supplementary section of the MSstats v4.0 paper, I made an annotation file where the 'subject' is my treatment (untreated v treated). I just wanted to check with you whether this is correct, please. I think my annotation file would just be looking at the time-point comparisons rather than the time-points/treatments comparisons?

Many thanks,
Amandeep

messages.subject: Re: Time-course study design annotation query
messages.body_plain:
Hi Amandeep,

You're on the right track here.  I made adjustments to your annotation file and attached it as your original PPT.

Based on your experimental design, you can create more specific conditions, like "time_treatment", and then use contrast matrices (see slide 2) to still make comparisons between different timepoints.  By incorporating treatment into your condition, you're able to block on treatment (see slide 3) when making comparisons between different timepoints, which should increase your power (assuming your treatment has an effect on protein abundance).

Thanks,
Tony

Hello, I would like to analyze data using MSstats.

My data is TMT11 data. I performed the search using SpectraST and quantification using Libra in TPP, then converted the results to CSV format. My results contain the intensity of each channel. Can I use MSstats to analyze my results? If I want to manually modify the result file to make its format compatible with MSstats, how should I do it? Are there any functions in MSstats that can be used for this purpose?

Thanks a lot for your help.

messages.subject_clean: Data Format Conversion Inquiry for MSstats Compatibility
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Unfortunately we do not currently have a converter for your output. I would recommend checking out some of the example data included in the MSstatsTMT package to get an idea of the format you will need to convert your data into. The resulting dataset below should be a good place to start. You will need to extract the columns listed input.mq <http://input.mq>. Let me know if you run into trouble.

Devon

```
head(evidence)
head(proteinGroups)
head(annotation.mq <http://annotation.mq>)
input.mq <http://input.mq> <- MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat(evidence, proteinGroups, annotation.mq <http://annotation.mq>)
head(input.mq <http://input.mq>)
```

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am really interested in the use R package MSstatsPTM for the data analysis of a project we are currently working on in our lab.

I’m working with MaxQuant output and trying to load the data using MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat, but I’ve encountered some difficulties.
Initially, I received the following error from R:

Error in .checkAnnotation(annotation, labeling_type) :   Extra columns included in the annotation file that are not required.     This can cause problems in the converter dependencies. Please     only include the following columns in the annotation file:                  Run, Raw.file, Condition, BioReplicate, IsotopeLabelType

After that, I created an annotation file containing only the required columns, but then encountered a new error:
Error in .handleFractionsLF(input) :   ** MSstats suspects that there are fractionations and potentially technical replicates too. Please add Fraction column to the input.

If I try to remove the Fraction column, I receive the first error.

Would it be possible to kindly ask for your help in troubleshooting this issue? If helpful, I’d be happy to share the annotation file I prepared.

Thanks in advance,

Clarissa
